title: Feedback quantity can flip the absorbability verdict for upstream steps in canal pools: code and data for a controlled numerical counterexample

creators.name: Zhang, Xu
creators.affiliation: School of Water Conservancy and Hydropower Engineering, Hebei University of Engineering, Handan 056038, China

description:
Reproduction package for the manuscript Feedback quantity can flip the absorbability verdict for upstream steps in canal pools: a controlled numerical counterexample (submitted to Journal of Hydroinformatics, IWA Publishing).

Contents: a 1D Saint-Venant solver, a lumped 0D storage model with the A1/A3 decision rules, the canal controller with the two contrasted feedback quantities (pool-mean level and gate-adjacent single point), an independent replication in EPA SWMM 5.2 driven through pyswmm, a 25.6 km real reach parameterised from published data, every archived JSON/CSV result, and the figure scripts.

The central claim the package supports: holding the pool, the controller law, the gains, the setpoint and the disturbance fixed, and changing only the feedback measurement operator, flips the absorbability verdict (pool-mean peak 75.0 mm, A1) versus (gate-adjacent peak 470.8 mm, A3). The verdict pair is reproduced by EPA SWMM at every tested grid resolution.

Code is MIT licensed; data, results and figures are CC BY 4.0.
notes: Decision codes: A1 = absorbable within the ±150 mm band, A3 = non-absorbable / degrade. The BM-01 case is a synthetic reduced-model benchmark, not a calibrated model of a specific canal.
